subject: Banking
title: What DeFi Actually Does
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What DeFi Actually Does.

hook.text: DeFi lets you lend, borrow, and trade without a bank. Smart contracts on blockchains replace human intermediaries.

buildup.text: In traditional finance, a bank verifies your identity, holds your funds, and processes transactions.

discovery.text: Aave and Compound let users earn interest by depositing crypto. Borrowers post collateral and get instant loans.

twist.text: DeFi peaked at $180 billion in 2021 then crashed to $40 billion. Hacks, scams, and collapsing tokens wiped out fortunes.

climax.text: DeFi proved that banking without banks is technically possible. Whether it is safe, fair, or useful remains unproven.

punchline.text: Banking without banks. Technically possible, practically risky.

quiz.question: What caused DeFi to crash from $180 billion to $40 billion?
options: Hacks, scams, and collapsing token values

details.summary: Decentralized finance uses blockchain smart contracts to replicate banking services like lending, borrowing, and trading without traditional intermediaries. Users interact directly with code-based protocols instead of banks.
details.whyItMatters: DeFi demonstrates that banking functions can operate without banks. While still niche and risky, DeFi protocols have processed trillions in transactions and proven that code can replace institutional intermediaries for basic functions.
takeaways: DeFi protocols handle lending, borrowing, and trading via smart contracts
Total value locked in DeFi has exceeded 100 billion dollars
Smart contract bugs and hacks have caused billions in losses

faq.question: How does DeFi lending work without a bank?
faq.answer: Lenders deposit crypto into a smart contract pool. Borrowers put up collateral and withdraw from the pool. Interest rates adjust algorithmically based on supply and demand. No human approval, credit check, or bank is involved.

faq.question: Is DeFi safe enough for mainstream use?
faq.answer: Not yet. Smart contract vulnerabilities have been exploited for billions in theft. There is no deposit insurance, no customer support, and no recourse if things go wrong. The technology must mature significantly before mainstream adoption.
